result.summary: Encapsulates HTTP request state transitions by removing HTTPRequest::SetState and making individual parsing subroutines private. A unified HTTPRequest::Load method now drives parsing stages and manages internal state progression. In HTTPRemoteClient, request reading is flattened into a private non-static member method.
result.problem: After PR 35829 made HTTPRequest fields private, any caller holding a reference to a request could still arbitrarily mutate its internal state enum via SetState. Callers also had to manually invoke separate parsing methods for control data, headers, and body.
evidence: PR description notes that PR 35829 left an encapsulation gap: '#35829 made the fields of HTTPRequest & HTTPRemoteClient private, but still allows anyone with a reference to a request to update the internal state enum' citing PR review discussion (bitcoin/bitcoin#35829#discussion_r3860447518).
result.scope_notes: A significant portion of the diff consists of mechanical updates to unit tests and the fuzz target to use the new unified HTTPRequest::Load interface instead of the privatized step-by-step methods.
result.changed_since_previous: No substantive changes to the approach or scope; the refactoring logic and commit structure remain the same.
result.card: This pull request refactors the HTTP request parser by removing HTTPRequest::SetState, making individual parsing methods private, and introducing a single HTTPRequest::Load entry point to handle state transitions internally. It addresses an encapsulation gap noted in review on PR 35829 where external callers could arbitrarily mutate request state. Additionally, HTTPRemoteClient::ReadRequest is flattened into a non-static helper. The change is an internal refactor with no behavioral changes or open PR dependencies.

risk.why: Flaws in HTTP request parsing could cause valid RPC or REST requests to fail, hang, or prematurely disconnect clients.
